title: Senior Financial Controller (Xero) — Rebuild & Own the Finance Function of a Fast-Scaling E-commerce Brand
job_title: Senior Financial Controller (Xero) — Rebuild & Own the Finance Function of a Fast-Scaling E-commerce Brand
description: We're an Australian premium e-commerce retailer — pool tables, arcade machines, pinball, kegerators, saunas and more. We do $10M in revenue and we're scaling to $40M over the next two years. We run our own warehousing, national delivery and an installation team. We're ambitious, we move fast, and we are dead serious about fixing our finance function properly this time. We're looking for a Senior Financial Controller to take full ownership of our books, rebuild our Xero from the ground up, and turn it into the system the business actually steers by. This is a long-term, full-time, ongoing role. It is not a project, not a tidy-up, and not a part-time advisory seat. READ THIS BEFORE APPLYING — WE'RE BEING COMPLETELY STRAIGHT WITH YOU Our books are not in good shape, and we're not going to pretend otherwise. Xero is disconnected from our inventory system. Our cost of goods is inflated and nobody can fully explain why. Our chart of accounts can't show us profit by product category or by department. We've had two bookkeepers and two senior finance people through this business and the books are no better than a year ago. We have strong data sitting in our other systems — Shopify, Unleashed, Polar Analytics — but nothing ties together in Xero, and Xero is not currently a source of truth. We are telling you this upfront because we want someone who reads that and gets interested, not nervous. If untangling a genuine mess and building order out of it is the work you're best at and enjoy most, keep reading. If you want a clean set of books to gently maintain, this is the wrong role and we'll both know it quickly. WHAT THIS ROLE ACTUALLY IS You will own the finance function. Not assist it — own it. In your first months the job is heavy reconstruction: you will pull apart what's wrong, rebuild the Xero chart of accounts properly, and rebuild trust in every number. Once it's clean, you run it — month-end, management accounts, cash flow, reporting — and you keep it immaculate. You'll work directly with the CEO and closely with our operations team, and you'll be the person who can answer, with confidence and evidence, “are we actually making money, and where?” WHAT YOU'LL DELIVER The headline outcomes we are hiring you to produce: - Xero rebuilt as the single source of truth — a clean, correctly structured chart of accounts the leadership team trusts without second-guessing. - Profit visibility by product category — pool tables, arcade, pinball, kegerators, dartboards, LED and furniture — so we finally know which categories make money and which don't. This is a build and depends on cost inputs being cleaned up over time; you'll be central to getting there. - Departmental P&L — cost-centre reporting so marketing, sales, operations and admin can each see and own their numbers. - Reliable month-end — a full close and management accounts the business can make real decisions on, every month, on time. - A 13-week rolling cash flow forecast — we have seasonal revenue and financing facilities; we need to see cash coming before it becomes a problem. WHAT YOU'LL OWN DAY TO DAY - Rebuilding and maintaining the Xero chart of accounts and tracking-code structure. - Untangling cost of goods — core stock vs drop-ship, freight-in vs freight-out, installation costs, merchant fees, and the inventory adjustment journals currently muddying the picture. - Owning the reconciliation of data flowing from Shopify and our inventory system (Unleashed) into Xero, with no unexplained variances. Our operations team owns the inventory system itself — you are the person who makes sure it reconciles cleanly into the books. - The full month-end close and management accounts. - The 13-week cash flow view and tracking of our financing facilities. - Bank reconciliation, accounts payable, supplier invoice processing and payment run preparation. - Feeding clean, reliable data to our external Australian tax accountant, who handles tax, GST and BAS. WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR - This is a senior role and we need a senior person. Specifically: - 6+ years in accounting or finance, with real depth in e-commerce, retail or inventory-heavy businesses. - Genuine Xero mastery — you have personally restructured a chart of accounts and built a tracking-code framework, not just worked inside one someone else set up. Xero certification expected or close to it. - A demonstrable track record of taking messy, untrusted books and making them clean and reliable — this is the single most important thing we're hiring for. - Strong command of inventory and cost-of-goods accounting — you understand how landed cost, stock and COGS move through the books. - Confident building cost-centre and category-level reporting from scratch. - Hands-on with Shopify and an inventory/ERP system (Unleashed or similar). - Self-directed and accountable — you own outcomes, surface problems early, and don't need chasing. - Excellent written and spoken English, and genuinely confident leading a conversation on a weekly video call with the CEO. - A reliable internet connection, a quiet space for video calls, and solid working overlap with Australian Eastern time (AEST). WHAT'S IN IT FOR THE RIGHT PERSON - Full ownership of a finance function from day one — this is your domain to build. - A genuine path to a senior finance leadership seat as we scale toward $40M; we want this person to grow with us. - A long-term, stable, full-time role with a business that's serious about getting this right and will back you to do it. - A proper handover and structured onboarding — you will not be dropped in cold. - Direct line to the CEO; your work will visibly drive how the business makes decisions. - Paid local Philippine public holidays and a genuine commitment to a long-term working relationship. HOW TO APPLY Applications must be submitted through our application form. Applications that come only as a message here, without the form completed, will not be reviewed. Apply here: ---------- We're interviewing immediately and moving quickly for the right person.

title: Sign Industry Estimator
description: **MUST BE AVAILABLE MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY 8am-4pm MST Position Overview We are a custom sign manufacturing and installation company seeking an experienced Estimator to join our team remotely. In this role, you will read and interpret architectural and shop drawings, develop accurate cost estimates, and build winning bids for interior and exterior sign projects ranging from single-tenant signage to multi-location rollouts. You will work closely with sales, project managers, fabrication, and installation crews to ensure every estimate reflects true scope, true cost, and a margin we can stand behind. The right candidate is detail-obsessed, deadline-driven, and comfortable owning the numbers from takeoff through bid handoff. Key Responsibilities • Read and interpret drawings: Review architectural plans, elevations, site plans, shop drawings, electrical drawings, and landlord/municipal sign criteria packages to define accurate scope. • Perform quantity takeoffs: Extract material types, square footage, linear footage, hardware counts, and electrical specs from drawings and RFP documents. • Build complete estimates: Price materials, fabrication labor, finishing, freight, permitting, engineering, installation labor, equipment (lifts, cranes, traffic control), and applicable markups. • Specify installation scope: Determine mounting methods, wall conditions, electrical requirements, lift or crane needs, permitting obligations, and crew sizing for both interior and exterior installs. • Source and quote vendors: Solicit and evaluate quotes from material suppliers, sub-fabricators, electrical sign manufacturers, permit runners, and installation subcontractors. • Maintain pricing data: Work with Purchasing to ensure material, labor, and burden rates are current • Produce bid documents: Deliver clean, client-ready proposals with clear scope, inclusions, exclusions, assumptions, lead times, and payment terms. • Collaborate cross-functionally: Work with sales on pursuit strategy, with production on buildability, and with project managers on smooth job handoff after award. • Track and analyze: Maintain a bid log, hit-rate tracking, and post-job cost reviews to continuously sharpen estimating accuracy. Required Qualifications • Sign industry experience: 3+ years estimating in custom signage (channel letters, monuments, pylons, wayfinding, ADA, dimensional, vinyl/graphics, and electrical signage). • Drawing literacy: Demonstrated ability to read architectural drawings, shop drawings, electrical schematics, and sign criteria packages without hand-holding. • Pricing fluency: Strong working knowledge of sign materials (aluminum, acrylic, LEDs, power supplies, vinyl, hardware), fabrication processes, finishes, and labor burden. • Installation knowledge: Practical understanding of interior and exterior install methods, wall types, mounting hardware, electrical hookup, lifts, cranes, and permitting workflows. • Excel proficiency: Comfortable with formulas, lookups (VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP/INDEX-MATCH), pivot tables, and conditional logic; able to build and maintain estimating workbooks. • ERP software: Hands-on experience with an ERP or job costing system (e.g., CYRIOUS Control, Shopify Sign, NetSuite, Sage, or similar). Preferred Qualifications • Experience in estimating national rollouts or multi-site programs. • Familiarity with UL listing requirements for electric signs. • Working knowledge of local permitting processes and landlord criteria packages. • Bluebeam, AutoCAD, or other PDF/CAD markup experience. • Background in fabrication, project management, or field installation before moving into estimating. What Success Looks Like in This Role • Estimates are accurate, complete, and submitted on or before deadline. • Bid hit rate improves quarter-over-quarter without margin erosion. • Post-job cost variance stays within target on awarded work. • Sales, production, and installation teams trust the numbers and the scope handoff. description: TITLE: Part-Time Bookkeeper + Cash Flow / Finance Manager (QuickBooks Online) - Remote HOURS: Part-time to start (20-25 hrs/week), with opportunity to grow into full-time Must overlap 2-3 hours with Vancouver, Canada (PST) START: ASAP PAY: Competitive and based on experience. We pay for quality. ABOUT US: We are a Vancouver, Canada-based high-end residential construction supplier and installer (project-based). We work on luxury custom homes and manage large project invoices, deposits, progress payments, and job costs. This is a serious role. We are not looking for a generic VA. We are looking for a real accounting professional who can take ownership of our bookkeeping and help manage the overall financial health of the company. We are looking for someone long-term. If you are looking for short-term work, freelancing, or multiple clients, this role is not a good fit. We want someone who will become part of the company for years, grow with us, and be treated like part of the team. ROLE SUMMARY: You will be responsible for keeping our accounting clean and accurate in QuickBooks Online, ensuring reconciliations are done properly, tracking job profitability, and maintaining cash flow visibility for the owner. Our transaction volume is not huge, but our invoices are large and accuracy is extremely important. RESPONSIBILITIES: QuickBooks Online bookkeeping and cleanup. Bank and credit card reconciliations. Accounts payable and accounts receivable. Transaction categorization and proper coding. Maintaining a clean chart of accounts and organized records. Tracking income and costs by job/project (job costing). Tracking deposits and progress payments correctly. Monitoring job profitability while projects are active. Maintaining a cash flow statement and identifying cash flow risks early. Providing a simple monthly financial health summary to the owner. Monthly reporting including Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, AR Aging, cash summary, and basic job margin snapshot. Preparing clean year-end records for our external accountant. Supporting GST/PST preparation (Canada). Guidance will be provided. REQUIREMENTS (STRICT): Strong QuickBooks Online experience. Strong reconciliation skills. Month-end close experience. Experience preparing financial reports. Strong English communication (written and spoken). High attention to detail and strong follow-through. Professionalism and confidentiality. PREFERRED (STRONGLY): Construction or project-based accounting experience. Job costing experience. Audit, controller, or accounting manager experience. Buildertrend or similar software experience BENEFITS: Long-term stable role. Part-time to start with growth to full-time. Two weeks paid vacation per year (once full-time). Respectful, professional working environment. Clear expectations and communication. IMPORTANT: HOW TO APPLY (READ CAREFULLY) Applications that do not follow instructions will be ignored. We are using this process to filter applicants who are serious and detail-oriented. STEP 1: Write this at the top of your application: I READ THE INSTRUCTIONS STEP 2: Answer these questions in writing: Explain step-by-step how you reconcile a bank account in QuickBooks Online. Explain your month-end close process in checklist style. Video can be Loom, Google Drive, or YouTube unlisted. OPTIONAL BONUS: Attach a screenshot of a bank reconciliation screen you personally completed in QuickBooks Online. Blur all confidential information. FINAL NOTE: If your profile includes unrelated services such as social media, graphic design, video editing, or lead generation, we will assume accounting is not your main skill. We are looking for an accounting professional who takes this role seriously.

title: Shopify E-Commerce Finance Controller — P&L, ROAS & Cashflow for a 12-Store Dropshipping Group
job_title: Shopify E-Commerce Finance Controller — P&L, ROAS & Cashflow for a 12-Store Dropshipping Group
description: Summary Shopify E-Commerce Finance Controller — Daily Store P&L, ROAS & Cashflow Reconciliation for a 12-Store Dropshipping Group (Proactive, Self-Directing) Intro We run a portfolio of around 12 Shopify dropshipping stores across two entities (Netherlands and US), scaling toward roughly €25M this year. We need someone who lives and breathes Shopify store economics — daily revenue, COGS, ad spend, ROAS, payment fees and refunds — and who can make every store's P&L tie out to the actual cash landing in our accounts. If you have run the numbers behind Shopify dropshipping stores before, this will feel familiar. If you have only done traditional bookkeeping, it will not. About us We operate a growing portfolio of Shopify dropshipping stores in fashion and home décor. We launch, scale and sell individual stores, so each one is run as a standalone business unit with its own daily P&L — and each one has to stay sale-ready, meaning a buyer can review clean store-level financials at any ---------- nt. Quiet months run €400K–500K; Black Friday peaks hit €1M–2M. We buy traffic primarily through Google Ads (and Pinterest on some stores), fulfil through a 3PL partner, and run a multi-provider payment stack. What you'll do Own the daily P&L for each Shopify store — either filling it directly or coordinating the tea ---------- mber(s) who do, while owning the accuracy either way. Each daily row tracks: Revenue, COGS, Google Adspend, Mediabuying fee, transaction/payment provider fee, refunds, and the resulting Profit, ROAS, Profit %, COGS % and CVR % Pull supplier and fulfilment invoices from Slack daily and book accurate COGS per store (product + shipping + fulfilment, often combined on one invoice) Reconcile daily ad spend pulled from the Google Ads and Pinterest accounts against what is logged in each store P&L, and against Shopify revenue and order counts Track real payment provider fees and payout timing across Shopify Payments, multiple PayPal accounts, PayPal Hong Kong, WOP Payments, Ocean Payments and Airwallex — not estimates Catch the leaks that distort dropshipping P&Ls: refunds processed through old/disconnected PayPal accounts, chargebacks and dispute fees, FX conversion costs (EUR/USD/HKD), and payout delays — and make the internal P&L reconcile to actual bank cash Build and own weekly, monthly and quarterly reporting per store and per entity Evolve our current daily P&L template into a complete, sale-ready store-level reporting standard Coordinate the existing operational finance team (payments processing and invoice control) What we're looking for Hands-on experience running or controlling the financials of Shopify (or comparable DTC) e-commerce stores — this is a hard requirement You understand store-level unit economics: ROAS, AOV, CVR, COGS %, blended margin, and how ad spend, refunds and payment fees move the real profit number Comfortable pulling and reconciling data from Shopify, Google Ads, and multiple payment providers in multiple currencies Strong reconciliation discipline — you know why reported profit and bank cash diverge in an e-commerce business, and how to close the gap Reliable async communicator inside a remote international team Nice to have Dropshipping / 3PL fulfilment invoicing experience Experience preparing store-level financials for a sale or due diligence (we sell stores) Yuki (NL) and/or Xero (US) experience Experience automating Shopify/ad-account/payment-provider data into reporting The mindset that matters most We have worked with bookkeepers who fill cells correctly and stop there. That is not enough for a fast-moving store portfolio. We want someone who notices a store's COGS % drifting and digs into why, who spots a refund leak through an old PayPal account before it eats a month of margin, and who proposes and builds improvements to the reporting system on their own initiative. You should be the person who makes the numbers trustworthy without being asked twice. How to apply Start your application with the word RECONCILED so we know you read the full post. Then answer briefly: Which Shopify or DTC stores' financials have you run or controlled? Give revenue scale and your exact role. Walk us through how you would find and close a gap between a store's reported P&L profit and the actual cash in the bank. Would you prefer to do the daily store P&L hands-on, coordinate a team that does it, or both — and why?

title: Senior US Tax Reviewer (UltraTax/CCH) — Full-Time
description: About Whyte CPA P.C. We're a virtual CPA firm in Gilbert, Arizona serving about 60 monthly clients. Our niche is S-corporation owners and real estate investors. Small firm, lean operation, high standards on the work that goes out the door. The owner currently does all final review and signs every return. That bottleneck is why this role exists. We need a senior reviewer who hits the ground running and produces output clean enough that the owner's final pass is a 10-minute confirmation, not real review work. What You'll Actually Do This is a year-round, full-time, review-first role. Here's what you'll spend your time on: Tax return review. Federal and state returns prepared by staff. Heavy on 1040s with K-1s, 1120Ss, partnerships, and 1041s. Most returns include K-1s coming in (most prepared by us), Schedule E with rentals, brokerage statements, and frequently a Schedule C or Schedule E pg 1. These are not generic 1040s. You catch errors, identify missed positions, flag judgment calls, and write clear review notes back to the preparer. Bookkeeping review (monthly). QBO books prepared by staff each month. You don't do bookkeeping — but you must be able to review it at a senior level. You identify reconciliation issues, miscoded transactions, and items affecting tax planning before the books feed into planning workups. Quarterly tax planning review. Staff prepares projections in UltraTax's tax planner using annualized financials. You review for accuracy, identify missed strategies, and flag unreasonable assumptions before the work reaches the owner and client. You may also handle some planning prep directly on the most complex clients, or step in when staff bandwidth is tight. IRS and state tax authority correspondence. Notice review, research, and drafting responses. Volume is low (a few per month). Routine notices (math errors, balance due, missing forms) you handle end-to-end. Complex resolution work (payment plans, penalty abatement, audits, OICs, appeals) is collaborative — you bring the research and reasoning, we work through the approach together, owner reviews and signs. We don't expect deep OIC or appeals experience on day one. We expect a strong thinker who can learn the procedures. Owner holds representation authority before the IRS; EA credential is a plus but not required. IRS Solutions Software is used for transcripts and case management. Complex return prep. Most prep work is handled by staff. You'll prepare returns yourself when they require senior-level judgment from prep through completion, or when staff bandwidth is tight. This is not the bulk of your time, but it will happen, and we want someone who treats it as part of the role rather than an exception. New service lines we may build together. We're exploring bringing cost segregation studies in-house and may add other advisory work over time. We're not looking for someone who has done it all before — we're looking for someone who can think critically, learn alongside us, and bring solutions rather than problems. Who You Are You have 5–7 years of US tax experience, with 2–3 years specifically in a review capacity — not just preparation. Be ready to talk about the difference. A preparer who started reviewing six months ago is not what we're looking for. A preparer for three years who has been reviewing for three years is. You have hands-on experience with UltraTax CS, CCH Axcess, Lacerte, or ProConnect. You know S-corp work concretely: basis tracking, §199A computation, reasonable comp analysis, distributions vs. wages. Partnership review experience is a strong plus. You write in clear, professional English (C1 or C2). Review notes need to be actionable for the preparer. Client communications need to land cleanly with US clients. You are detail-oriented and self-policing. When you don't know something, you say so and look it up rather than guessing. You flag your own uncertainty before someone has to ask. You are comfortable with AI-augmented workflows. Our review process uses Claude and TaxGPT alongside human judgment. The AI workflow is firm standard, not optional. Strong candidates are either already using AI tools in their work or genuinely curious to learn. Candidates who view AI as a gimmick or want to skip it on "easy" returns are not a fit. You are self-directed in a remote-first environment. The owner travels for portions of the year and your time zone overlap will shift accordingly. We need someone who can run the review function with minimal oversight, not someone who needs daily check-ins to stay on track. Real estate experience (rentals, short-term rentals, cost segregation, 1031 exchanges) is helpful but not required. We can teach the niche; we can't teach review judgment. Software Stack Required: UltraTax CS (preferred) or CCH Axcess, TaxDome, QuickBooks Online Acceptable in place of UltraTax: Lacerte or ProConnect with willingness to learn UltraTax Not acceptable: Drake-only experience Used in workflow: Claude Pro, TaxGPT (Agent Andrew), IRS Solutions, Excel, Adobe Acrobat Pro If your tax software experience is Drake only, please don't apply. We're not the right fit. Compensation Detail Base salary: $3,800/month USD (paid twice monthly via Wise, on time, every time) 13th month: $3,800 paid in December, prorated for partial first year Internet stipend: $50/month Total annual comp: $50,000 USD Hours: Full-time. Compensation is salary — you are not paid hourly or for overtime. The expectation is that work gets done at high quality. During tax season (Feb 1–April 15), expect 50–55 hour weeks. In off-season, you manage your own time as long as work is current and communication is maintained. Tax season support: One long weekend (Friday–Sunday) off during tax season, scheduled with two weeks notice, to maintain consistent quality. Philippine holidays: All standard PH public holidays observed and paid. No work expected. Off-season flexibility: Take time when work is slow. We don't track formal PTO. Work gets done, communication is maintained, time is yours to manage. Negotiation: Base may be increased to $4,000/month for an exceptional candidate after the test process. Hiring Process 1. Application — Submit per the instructions below. Generic applications are discarded immediately. 2. First screen — 30-minute video call with the owner. 3. Paid test return — One real return (sanitized client data), $400 USD, ~3–4 hours of your time, due within 7 days. You produce review notes in your own format using your own workflow. We're testing your judgment, not your ability to follow our SOP. 4. Judgment interview — 30-minute call discussing your test return, plus 2–3 scenario questions about how you'd handle specific review situations. 5. Reference check — One reference from a recent supervisor or peer reviewer who can speak to your work. 6. Offer Total process: 2–3 weeks for serious candidates. How to Apply Send your application with the subject line: "Senior Reviewer — [Your Full Name]" Include the following in the body. If your application doesn't follow this structure, we'll assume you didn't read the post and won't respond. 1. Experience summary (3–5 sentences): Your years in US tax, your years specifically in a review capacity, the type of firm you've worked at (US firm, mid-tier PH outsourcing operation, etc.), and the volume/type of returns you've reviewed. 2. Tax software: Which of UltraTax CS, CCH Axcess, Lacerte, ProConnect have you used? For each, name the specific modules (1040, 1120S, 1065, 1041) and roughly how many returns you've worked in each. 3. DISC scores (if available). If you haven't taken DISC, OnlineJobs.ph has a free 10-minute test — please take it before applying. 4. A specific review catch you're proud of (2–3 sentences): What was the issue, how did you find it, what was the correction, what would have happened if it shipped uncaught. Specific and technical, not abstract. 5. AI in your workflow (2–3 sentences): How do you currently use Claude, ChatGPT, or other AI tools in your tax work? If you don't currently use them, how would you approach learning a firm's AI-augmented review process? 6. Availability: Earliest start date and any current employment that would need to transition. We're hiring for fit, not speed. Process moves quickly for serious applicants — but we'll wait for the right person. What This Role Is Not — Not part-time or seasonal — Not for someone learning US tax (you should already know it) — Not a stepping stone to bigger firms — we want someone who wants to settle in We're looking forward to hearing from you.
